text: IAM is AWS's global identity and access management service — global meaning it isn't scoped to a Region at all. An IAM user or role you create is available account-wide.

Four core entities: users are long-term identities, groups collect users for bulk policy assignment, roles are temporary identities anything can assume, and policies are the JSON documents that grant or deny permissions.

A role is different from a user in one crucial way — nothing owns its credentials long-term. A Lambda function reading from S3 gets a temporary, auto-rotated execution role instead of hardcoded access keys.
That's least privilege in practice: the minimum permissions actually needed. Next up: EC2 and Lambda, AWS's core compute services.
